subject.title: Feature request: first-class async result routing back to originating topic sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add this as a core async route registry, expose plugin/API seams so a plugin can own it, or defer it as too broad for core right now?
rationale: The request is coherent but it chooses product boundaries, storage, privacy, safety, and extension APIs; code inspection shows current primitives are insufficient but no narrow bug fix owns the full shape.

options.title: Design plugin/API-backed v1
options.body: Define the route registry, matcher, storage, privacy, and approval contracts first while keeping source-specific watchers and integrations outside core when existing plugin seams suffice.

options.title: Build core Gateway registry
options.body: Accept a larger core feature with SQLite-backed state, route lifecycle APIs, matcher interfaces, and tests for visible delivery, dedupe, ambiguity, and approval policy.

options.title: Defer to local/plugin workflows
options.body: Keep the existing hook, heartbeat, cron, and targeted wake primitives as the supported path until stronger demand or a missing plugin API is identified.

recommendation.title: Design plugin/API-backed v1
recommendation.body: Define the route registry, matcher, storage, privacy, and approval contracts first while keeping source-specific watchers and integrations outside core when existing plugin seams suffice.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily product/API boundary and storage policy, and this person is the strongest available routing candidate from recent session-key architecture history.
